why: The two spellings differ only when the phase's entry EQUALS the reference's, and then both windows -- [at, at+2] and [at-2, at] -- contain `at`, whose distance is zero.  So both take the exact-match arm, both leave `bestAt` at an index whose entry equals the value, and both stores write that value back over itself.  Both also leave the second-nearest at 32,256 or below, because the demotion at the final (zero-distance) improvement writes the nearest, which is at most the sentinel; and the second-nearest never rises again, since the demotion writes a value at most the sentinel and the else-if writes a strictly smaller one.  The only reader is the ratio, and it can only differ between the two while the nearest is still its sentinel -- any iteration that improves rewrites the second-nearest to 32,256 at its first improvement and then evolves identically over an identical window -- which needs a second-nearest above 64,512.  Unreachable after the equality that caused the difference.  Finding 1433.

second study: divide instead of multiplying by the reciprocal
why: Both operands are `(float)` of the magnitude of a difference of two shorts, so both are exact integers in 0..65535.  |second/nearest - 2| is either 0 -- when second == 2 * nearest -- or at least 1/nearest >= 1/65535 = 1.5e-5, which is ten orders of magnitude above the difference between the two spellings, so only second == 2 * nearest can separate them.  Confirmed once by exhausting all 32,767 such pairs in a throwaway program built -m32 -O2 -mfpmath=387, so that the intermediates stay in x87 registers as they do here: no separator.  fl(1/n) is within 2^-64 relative of 1/n and the spacing of extended-precision values at 2 is 2^-62, so 2*fl(1/n)*n rounds to exactly 2.0 for every n.  Finding 1433.

label: second study: drop the guard on an exact match
why: A nearest distance of zero means some k gave |v - linMapp[unSuspectedPhase][from + k]| == 0 and set `bestAt` to that k -- no later k can improve on zero, and nothing writes `linMapp` inside the (code, phase) iteration -- so `linMapp[unSuspectedPhase][bestAt]` still equals `linMapp[phase][at]` at the store and the repair writes the value back over itself.  Without the guard the ratio is (1/0) * second: +inf when second > 0, which repairs, and a NaN when second is 0 or a NaN, which does not.  Both outcomes are the same self-store, and neither `second` nor `bestAt` depends on the decision.  Finding 1433.
